projects.title: Pro Gym Hub
projects.description: Gym and club management platform connecting clubs, trainers, and members. Handles subscriptions, progress tracking, and daily operations in one Laravel app.
projects.tech: PHP, Laravel, MySQL, HTML, CSS, JavaScript

highlights.title: Problem
highlights.text: Gyms were running memberships, trainers, and day-to-day operations across disconnected tools, which made subscriptions and progress hard to track in one place.

highlights.title: What I built
highlights.text: A Laravel app that connects clubs, trainers, and members. I worked on the MySQL schema, REST-style flows, and the screens used for subscriptions, progress tracking, and daily operations.

highlights.title: Outcome
highlights.text: One platform instead of scattered admin work. The project is the kind of full-stack delivery I later carried into Java and Angular work: clear data model, working UI, and team collaboration.

projects.title: Design Hive
projects.description: Community for designers to publish work and interact through profiles, messaging, likes, and comments. Built with Laravel and Ajax.

highlights.title: Problem
highlights.text: Designers needed a place to publish work and talk to each other without bolting together a profile page, a chat, and a feed as separate tools.

highlights.title: What I built
highlights.text: A Laravel community with profiles, messaging, likes, and comments. Ajax kept the interactions feeling immediate instead of full page reloads on every like or message.

highlights.title: Outcome
highlights.text: A complete social-style product from schema to UI. It shows I can ship user-facing features, not only CRUD admin screens.

projects.title: Giving Hands
projects.description: Web app that helps people in Jordan find and connect with charities. Placed 4th of 25+ teams at the Code for Good Hackathon.
projects.tech: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bootstrap, Local Storage

details.role: Hackathon team project · Code for Good

highlights.title: Problem
highlights.text: People in Jordan often did not know which charity to contact, or how to reach them quickly when they wanted to help.

highlights.title: What I built
highlights.text: A web app that lists charities and helps users find and connect with the right one. Built under hackathon time pressure with a small team.

highlights.title: Outcome
highlights.text: 4th place out of 25+ teams. The useful part for hiring is not the stack — it is shipping a real local problem under a deadline.

projects.title: Bright Future
projects.description: Graduation project supporting people with Down syndrome through educational content, services, and opportunities. Backend built with Java, Spring Boot, and SQL Server.
projects.tech: Spring Boot, Java, Maven, SQL Server

highlights.title: Problem
highlights.text: Families and people with Down syndrome needed a single place for educational content, related services, and opportunities, instead of scattered information.

highlights.title: What I built
highlights.text: The Java Spring Boot backend and SQL Server model behind that platform: APIs for content, services, and opportunities, structured for a real product rather than a demo controller.

highlights.title: Outcome
highlights.text: A working graduation service in the same family of tools I use at work today. The repository is private, so this page is the public write-up of what the project actually was.
